name: exp_minutes
what_changed:
Playing-time model v2, switched on with PM.PT=1; PT=0 gives back production v1 exactly. In v1, a player with status 'a' got P(play) as his raw share of the last 6 matches, so a player who played all 6 got 1.00, while only about 90% of those players actually play. v2 computes P(play) = (sum w*played + 0.5*0.5) / (sum w + 0.5), with w = 0.5^age over all of the player's earlier matches this season. This is exponential recency weighting plus a Beta(0.25, 0.25) prior. An ever-present player now gets about 0.90, and early rounds are shrunk automatically. q60 and ePlay use 0.8^age (age counted in matches) over his appearances instead of a flat last-6 share. For flagged players (status not 'a'), only appearances while fit are used, and the published availability still multiplies the result. The code and the per-player text are in model.js (edits marked [exp_minutes]).

Tried on TRAIN and NOT adopted (negative results):
(a) Beta prior on q60 (Q_A=1, Q_MU=0.7). Brier of P(60+|plays) improved by about 5% (0.160 -> 0.152 per fixture), but points MAE got worse (1.6184 -> 1.6222 and 1.6446 -> 1.6466).
(b) Logistic recalibration of P(play) using the recency 60+ rate. Brier of P(play) improved (0.1446 -> 0.1425 and 0.1499 -> 0.1477), minutes MAE improved (23.76 -> 23.08 and 23.40 -> 22.74), and minutes bias went from about -2.5 to about -1.1. Points MAE got worse (1.6292 and 1.6631). This was run on top of (a).
(c) The 'st' (started) column added almost nothing beyond the 60+ share. Per-fixture Brier: 0.1368 -> 0.1363 with st, 0.1353 with the 60+ rate. 'st' is also missing before GW16 in 2022-23.
(d) A previous-season appearance rate as the prior mean made Brier worse in 2023-24 (0.1378 -> 0.1412 and up), both overall and in rounds 4-8.

Because the final selection was made by TRAIN points MAE, the shipped config equals the one from this experiment's earlier run (archived in prev_attempt/), which this run re-verified.

Other TRAIN diagnostics:
- About 40-50% of the MAE gain is plain downward scaling. v2's mean prediction is about 8% lower. Scaling v1 to the same mean gives about 1.665 / 1.71, against v2's 1.618 / 1.644. Note that MAE keeps falling as you scale predictions down, so this metric rewards under-prediction.
- Players who played all of their last 6 matches: predicted P(play) 0.899 vs observed 0.908 (2022-23), 0.898 vs 0.900 (2023-24), 0.899 vs 0.907 (2024-25).
params: PT=1, PL_LAM=0.5, PL_A=0.5, PL_MU=0.5, Q_LAM=0.8 (all tuned on TRAIN by Brier of P(play) and by points MAE). Not adopted, kept only in model_variants.js: Q_A=1, Q_MU=0.7, PL_B=[0.325,0.786,0.285].
risks:
1) Injury interaction. The replay has no injury status, so the whole-season history includes injury absences, and the parameters were tuned with them in. Live, injuries are handled by FPL status and chance of playing.

Proxy check on TRAIN: I removed non-appearances that start an absence of 3+ matches, treating them as likely injuries. On those rows, v2 still clearly beats v1 on Brier (0.149 -> 0.134 in 2022-23, 0.158 -> 0.138 in 2023-24). But v2 under-predicts there: mean P 0.73 vs observed 0.82, and the top bin is 0.89 vs 0.93. So live, for status 'a' players, v2 is probably a few points too pessimistic.

The worst case is a player just back from injury: his recent injury zeros get the heaviest weights. For example, after a 4-match injury P(play) is about 0.15, against 0.33 in v1. Flagged players are not double-counted, because their pPlay0 uses only appearances while fit (about 0.9, meaning rotation risk only) and is then multiplied by the published chance.

A possible live-only fix, which the replay cannot validate: drop the zero-minute matches in a player's most recent absence of 3+ matches when he was flagged during it. That would need the site to log status history.

2) About half of the points-MAE gain comes from lower predictions overall. Bias moves from +0.05 to -0.11 on validation, and from -0.32 to -0.46 in 2022-23. Minutes are under-predicted by about 2.6-2.8 per row (v1 was about +1.1 to +1.5).

3) The Monte Carlo ranges shift: fewer near-certain starters, so ranges get a little wider.

4) Validation was looked at twice, both times with the same frozen config. The first look was this experiment's earlier run; the second was this run's re-check after TRAIN-only variant tests. No choice was made using validation.
ship_notes:
How to ship: copy the PM additions and the pmPlayer block marked [exp_minutes] from model.js. No extra data file is needed, because it uses only the current season's history.

The Monte Carlo simulation already draws plays ~ Bernoulli(pPlay) and 60+ ~ Bernoulli(q60), so it picks up the new rates directly, with no extra component.

Validation results for 2024-25, v1 -> v2:
- points MAE: 1.6936 -> 1.5879
- Brier of P(play): 0.1686 -> 0.1452
- minutes MAE: 23.22 -> 22.69
- MAE by position: GKP 1.978 -> 1.824, DEF 1.678 -> 1.598, MID 1.578 -> 1.471, FWD 2.092 -> 1.940

TRAIN results, v1 -> v2:
- 2022-23: MAE 1.6951 -> 1.6178, Brier 0.1680 -> 0.1446, minutes MAE 24.07 -> 23.59
- 2023-24: MAE 1.7659 -> 1.6442, Brier 0.1785 -> 0.1499, minutes MAE 24.38 -> 23.29

If calibrated playing-time probabilities matter more than points MAE, for example for the simulation ranges, consider the logistic recalibration variant PL_B instead. It gives better Brier and minutes MAE, and points MAE about 0.01-0.02 worse on TRAIN; it has not been evaluated on validation.
